title: pendingWork queue grows without bound and pins sessions against archival
description:
The pendingWork queue is append-only in practice. Nothing ever drains it, so it accumulates forever and distorts session resume.

Observed in this repo on 2026-07-27:
- 30 pendingWork entries, oldest created 2026-03-20 (over four months old)
- 13 of the 30 are generic placeholders: 8x "Capture work and prepare a clean handoff." and 5x "Continue previous handoff"
- only 18 distinct titles across 30 entries
- 30 distinct sessions are pinned against archival by these entries, while only 16 active session files exist

Mechanics:
1. startNewSession unshifts a new item onto pendingWork every time a session is superseded (src/core/state.ts, startNewSession). applyHandoff unshifts another when the session has next steps or blockers.
2. runSessionHygiene archives stale session FILES but never removes pendingWork entries, so the queue is unaffected by the 30 day sweep.
3. referencedSessionIds adds every item.carriedFromSession to the referenced set, and findArchiveCandidates skips referenced sessions. A pendingWork entry therefore pins its source session as active permanently, which defeats the hygiene policy it was meant to cooperate with.
4. inferSessionStart reads pendingWork[0] and seeds a resumed session from it with consumePendingWork, so only the single newest entry is ever consumed, and only on a cold start with no active session.

Observable damage: a cold start inherits whatever was interrupted most recently regardless of age or relevance. This is not theoretical. On 2026-07-27 a checkpoint recording the security audit fixes was merged into session-2026-07-11T02-35-58-242Z, a 16 day old session about an unrelated Kalshi trading app, because checkpointState reuses state.activeSession whenever one exists with no staleness or relevance check.

Related audit finding: toPendingWork collapses a whole session into four fields and keeps only nextSteps[0], dropping triedItems, assumptions, blockers, and regressionRisks. The anti-loop signal does not survive a session boundary in structured form. Any fix here should consider widening PendingWorkItem at the same time.

Not urgent and not a security issue. Lower priority than the audit High items (holistic-itm, holistic-lyd, holistic-jke) and M-6 (holistic-a9h), all now closed.
design:
Open design questions, since this is a policy decision rather than a straight bug fix:

1. Retention. Options: cap the queue (keep newest N), age out entries past a threshold (mirror the 30 day session hygiene window), or drop entries whose source session has already been archived. A cap is simplest and bounds growth deterministically.

2. Placeholder suppression. toPendingWork should probably not enqueue at all when the session has no real next step, since "Capture work and prepare a clean handoff." carries no information and accounts for 8 of the current 30 entries.

3. Break the archival pin. referencedSessionIds should stop treating a pendingWork entry as an unconditional reason to keep a session active, or pendingWork retention must run before findArchiveCandidates so the two policies agree. Today they contradict each other.

4. Relevance on resume. inferSessionStart takes pendingWork[0] regardless of age. It should skip or flag entries older than the hygiene window rather than silently seeding a months old objective. Separately, checkpointState should not merge into an arbitrarily stale activeSession without at least surfacing that it is doing so.

5. Carryover fidelity. Widen PendingWorkItem to carry triedItems, assumptions, blockers, and regressionRisks instead of only recommendedNextStep, so resume can rebuild real context. This is the higher value half of the work.

Suggested sequencing: 2 and 3 are small and independent. 1 is a one line policy once 3 is settled. 4 and 5 are the behavioral changes that need tests around resume and carryover.

Existing tests to keep green: the 30 day hygiene suite in tests/run-tests.ts already asserts that pendingWork pins a session against archival ("30 day hygiene archives stale unreferenced sessions and leaves referenced ones active" covers session-pending-1). Changing item 3 means updating that expectation deliberately, not incidentally.
close_reason: Queue bounded by age and count, placeholder entries suppressed, archival pin now expires with the entry, and carryover carries tried/assumptions/blockers/regressions

title: Upstream git-hook daemon auto-start into the generated hook templates
description:
This repo carries hand-written hooks and helper scripts that give a better zero-touch story than the shipped templates, but because they are hand-written they carry no HOLISTIC-MANAGED marker, so repair can never update them and the behaviour never reaches other users.

What exists locally today (not generated by Holistic):
- .holistic-local/system/start-holistic.sh and start-holistic.ps1: check daemon.pid, exit if the pid is alive, otherwise launch the daemon detached. The sh variant branches on uname to use powershell -WindowStyle Hidden under MINGW/MSYS/CYGWIN and nohup elsewhere.
- .holistic-local/system/start-andon.ps1: probes ports 4318 and 5173 with Get-NetTCPConnection and starts the API and dashboard only if nothing is listening, redirecting stdout and stderr to log files under .holistic-local.
- .git/hooks/post-commit and post-checkout call start-holistic.sh in the background so the daemon and Andon come up on any commit or branch switch, for whichever agent is driving.
- .git/hooks/post-commit additionally runs a checkpoint with the commit subject as status.
- .git/hooks/pre-push prints holistic status and the sync command instead of syncing.

Why it is worth upstreaming: "open the repo, start working" is the stated product north star, and a daemon that starts itself on the first git event is closer to that than requiring bootstrap to install an OS autostart entry. The port and pid probes already make it idempotent.
design:
Design questions to settle before coding, because parts of this conflict with existing deliberate decisions.

1. Checkpoint on commit contradicts the current template. renderGitHooks post-commit says "Intentionally do not create a new checkpoint here. The user may have just committed Holistic state and expects the tree to stay clean." The local hook does checkpoint on every commit. Both positions are defensible; pick one and record why. If checkpointing returns it should probably be opt-in via config rather than default, since it dirties the tree right after a commit.

2. Auto-start must be presence-detected, not assumed. Andon is source-only and absent from a published install; this is the same trap that made the daemon crash for every installed user (holistic-jke). The template must check that services/andon-api/src/server.ts and scripts/andon-runtime-writer.mjs exist, and must honour HOLISTIC_ANDON=0. Prefer reusing andonAvailability from src/daemon.ts rather than reimplementing the check in shell.

3. Keep it agent-agnostic. Per the repo hard rule, nothing here may branch on agent name. A git hook is inherently agent-neutral, which is an advantage over the per-agent hook configs, so this should stay in the git-hook layer rather than moving into any agent adapter.

4. Do not block the git operation. Launch detached and never wait. A commit must not hang because a port probe is slow.

5. Windows spawn rules already bit us once. npm.cmd cannot be spawned without a shell on modern Node (see the H-2 fix in daemon.ts and the cmd.exe wrapper in scripts/andon-dev.mjs). Any generated PowerShell that starts the dashboard must use the same approach.

6. Probing ports on Windows uses Get-NetTCPConnection, which is unavailable on older hosts and on POSIX. The daemon already has isPortFree in src/daemon.ts; prefer generating a script that shells into the CLI or the daemon rather than duplicating port logic per platform.

7. Absolute paths are baked into the local scripts. Generated artifacts already interpolate rootDir, so this is consistent, but repair must regenerate them after any repo move. That is already true of the other system scripts.

8. Opt-in surface. Suggest a config flag such as daemon.autoStartOnGitEvents, default false for a first release, so existing users do not suddenly get background processes launched by a commit.

Payoff: once generated, these hooks carry the HOLISTIC-MANAGED marker, so repair keeps them current. Today the local copies are frozen forever, which is the immediate reason for filing this.

Related: holistic-jke (daemon startup crashes), holistic-d9d (Andon service auto-start on repo open) overlaps and should probably be merged with or closed by this.

title: Worktree hook propagation: install per-agent turn hooks into active worktrees at install time

notes:
Depends on holistic-58k (state.json unification must land first so there is a single session to write turn_state into). For Claude: enumerate worktrees and write .claude/settings.json into each. The install_targets field in the adapter turn_hook_config (main + worktrees) drives which targets the installer writes to. The git post-checkout hook re-runs the installer when a new worktree is created.
REQUIRED SCHEMA ADDITION: turn_hook_config must include a required capability field declaring the agent's tier. Enum: realtime_hooks (agent has turn/tool hooks; full turn_hook_config required), session_lifecycle_only (agent supports startup/checkpoint/handoff but no turn hooks; turn_hook_config omitted), substrate_fallback (no usable hook; rely on the file-watcher floor; turn_hook_config omitted, substrate fallback documented). Per tier: realtime_hooks REQUIRES a populated turn_hook_config; the other two tiers FORBID it. The writer/dashboard renders status per tier: realtime_hooks = live running/waiting; the other two = degraded-but-correct (no false 'running'). This field makes full agent coverage structural: no adapter doc can be written that silently omits its turn-capability.

title: Marker-less adapter docs silently disable the data-driven turn-hook installer
description:
Found 2026-07-29 while activating holistic-7l0. All nine adapters in .holistic-local/context/adapters/ carry NO provenance marker. isUserAuthoredDoc (src/core/docs.ts:57) treats a file that has lost HOLISTIC-GENERATED as user-authored, so writeDerivedDocs skips every one of them. Consequence chain: the adapters never received the '## Capability' section (holistic-35y) or the '## Turn Hook Config' section (holistic-i3j) - each file still has only its original six headings - so parseTurnHookConfigFromDoc finds nothing, and installAllTurnHooks parses ZERO configs and is a complete silent no-op in this repo.

Confirmed live: re-running writeAndonHookScripts + installAllTurnHooks left ~/.gemini/settings.json byte-identical, still holding the pre-fix identity-less command. The turn hooks currently in ~/.gemini/settings.json and .claude/settings.json are stale leftovers from an earlier install and can never be upgraded or repaired through the normal path.

Evidence these are stale, not customized: the adapters lack BOTH newer sections and all nine are missing the marker uniformly, which is what a pre-feature generation looks like, not deliberate per-agent editing.

Fix must respect the regression rule (never unconditionally regenerate over a user-authored adapter). Options: (a) treat a marker-less file whose body matches a known shipped template as refreshable; (b) an explicit opt-in refresh (holistic repair --refresh-adapters) that re-stamps the marker; (c) at minimum, make the silence loud - installAllTurnHooks installing zero hooks, or an adapter whose profile declares realtime_hooks having no Turn Hook Config section, should surface a warning in repair/doctor output instead of succeeding quietly.

Blocks the live effect of holistic-7l0 (code and tests are green; the fix cannot reach the agent configs until adapters carry the section) and therefore holistic-p39.
close_reason: Fixed both locally and in the product. Local (option 1): re-stamped all nine marker-less adapters in .holistic-local and regenerated them - diff confirmed purely additive (0 lines removed across all nine), so they were stale generated files, not customisations. All nine regained '## Capability'; the two realtime_hooks agents regained '## Turn Hook Config'. Reinstall then upgraded the real configs in place: ~/.gemini/settings.json SessionStart+AfterTool now carry '-Agent gemini' and .claude/settings.json Stop/UserPromptSubmit/PostToolUse carry '-Agent claude', with all GSD hooks preserved. Product (option 3): installAllTurnHooks now returns {installedAgents, warnings} and warns when an adapter declares realtime_hooks with no Turn Hook Config, when a marker-less adapter predates the template (naming the fix command), and when zero hooks install from a non-empty adapter set; correctly hook-less tiers stay quiet so warnings keep meaning something. New opt-in 'holistic repair --refresh-adapters true' re-stamps marker-less adapters and refreshes them, never touching a HOLISTIC-USER-EDITED file. Verified end to end through the real CLI in a throwaway repo: stale adapters warn and install nothing; with the flag, 9 docs refresh and Checks gains 'turn-hooks'.

title: Runtime writer freshness gate ignores turn-state sidecar, silencing live sessions mid-turn

During long autonomous turns state.json ages past 20 min, the writer stops emitting heartbeats and lifecycle asserts, Mission Control ages the card cold and drops it, and Stop->waiting flips recorded in the sidecar are never asserted. Observed live 2026-07-28: work.started frozen during idle, card vanished, single needs_input at 03:30:13Z overridden by daemon-checkpoint-driven work.started. Fix: treat a fresh sidecar recordedAt as a session liveness signal in the freshness check.

title: Turn-state sidecar carries no agent or session identity; foreign turn signals are misattributed
description:
Live finding 2026-07-29 during the p39 Gemini test. .holistic-local/turn-state.json is ONE shared file per runtime dir holding only {turnState, recordedAt} - see .holistic-local/system/andon-turn-hook.ps1 line 48, which writes no agent and no sessionId. scripts/andon-runtime-writer.mjs then takes turnState from the sidecar (line 437) but agentName from asAgentName(session) i.e. activeSession.agent (lines 225/249/272/300/324). The two are decoupled, so ANY agent's turn signal is stamped with whatever agent owns the active session.

Three consequences:
1. Misattribution. A Gemini AfterTool signal renders as a claude card. Observed live: Mission Control showed Running/claude while a Gemini CLI session was working in the same repo.
2. Last-write-wins across concurrent agents. Two agents in one repo overwrite each other's turn state; 'Claude waiting while Gemini runs' is unrepresentable. p39's note works around this by requiring other sessions be idle, which is a test-condition patch over a design gap.
3. p39's acceptance criterion is unprovable as written: a Gemini AfterTool write is byte-identical to a Claude PostToolUse write, so no observation can attribute a running flip to Gemini.

Fix direction (must stay agent-agnostic per CLAUDE.local - no if-agent-equals-claude in core): the installer ALREADY generates per-agent hook scripts from adapter turn_hook_config data (holistic-i3j), so the generating agent identity is known at generate time. Either stamp agent+sessionId into the sidecar payload, or write per-agent sidecars (turn-state.<agent>.json); per-agent files also eliminate the last-write-wins collision. Writer then keys the turn signal to the matching session instead of the global active session. Sidecar name/shape should come from adapter data, not a core branch.

Regression watch to preserve: turn hooks must never write state.json; sidecar-only freshness must not resurrect abandoned sessions (isSessionFreshEnoughForRuntimeWriter must keep decaying when BOTH state.json and every sidecar are stale).
notes: Implemented and green (314 tests). Hook scripts now take an -Agent argument filled in by the installer from the adapter file name; each agent writes turn-state.<agent>.json carrying an agent field; the writer resolves the sidecar for the active session's agent only, and refuses a foreign agent's record for BOTH turnState and freshness. Legacy unsuffixed turn-state.json still readable as unattributed. applyTurnHookToConfig now REWRITES an existing identity-less command in place (the andon-turn-hook marker matches both old and new forms, so the previous skip-if-present logic would have frozen every existing install). Verified live against the generated PS1 with a cwd-less Gemini-style payload: gemini turn signal invisible to a claude session; claude waiting and gemini running held simultaneously; abandoned claude session NOT resurrected by gemini activity. Live activation blocked by holistic-72n (marker-less adapters make installAllTurnHooks a no-op in this repo).
close_reason: Turn signals are now attributable. Hook scripts take an -Agent argument filled in by the installer from the adapter file name; each agent writes turn-state.<agent>.json with an agent field; the writer resolves only the active session's agent and refuses a foreign record for both turnState and freshness. applyTurnHookToConfig rewrites identity-less commands in place, which was required for existing installs. Verified against the generated PS1 with a cwd-less Gemini-style payload: gemini's signal invisible to a claude session, claude=waiting and gemini=running coexist, abandoned claude session not resurrected by gemini activity. Live in this repo's real agent configs. 318 tests green.

title: Completed next steps are never retired, so the resume recap accumulates stale work
description:
recentFirstMerge prepends new next steps and keeps every earlier one, and nothing ever removes an item that has been done. After six checkpoints in one session the active session carries every next step ever recorded, including work completed hours earlier.

Observed at the end of the audit session: the recap listed H-4, H-5, M-8, M-9, holistic-92c, the loopback auth token, and the carryover gap as things to try next, when all of them were finished and closed in that same session. The genuinely outstanding items were first in the list, so the ordering is right, but a reader has no way to tell where current work ends and history begins.

This actively misleads the next agent, which is the exact failure the product exists to prevent. It is also the same class as the pendingWork growth fixed in holistic-11h: an append-only structure with no retirement path.

Options to weigh:
- A checkpoint flag to replace rather than merge next steps.
- Retire a next step when a later checkpoint records it under done, matched loosely.
- Cap the list and age out the tail, mirroring prunePendingWork.
- Fold into the planned supersession work, which already proposes marking an entry superseded rather than deleting it. That is the most coherent home, since a completed next step is precisely a superseded one.

Note the recap joins the whole list with semicolons into one line, so the length problem is amplified in the resume output and in buildResumeRecap.
notes: Live symptom worth attaching to this bead: Mission Control kept showing the objective 'holistic-p39 (3e): run Gemini CLI with GEMINI_API_KEY...' for hours after p39 was closed and work had moved to (and finished) holistic-qd4. The objective is captured once into the session record at session.started from the resume recap's current objective (nextSteps[0]) and never revised, so a long-lived session advertises whatever was current when it began. Retiring completed next steps needs to also refresh the active session's objective, or the board misreports what the agent is doing.

title: Agent blocked on a permission prompt still reports Running
description:
Observed live 2026-07-30 00:56: Mission Control showed 'Running' while the session was actually blocked on a tool-approval dialog ('Allow Claude to run Re-run full suite?'), i.e. idle and waiting on the human. The operator read this as the board lying about running.

Cause: the turn hook maps Stop -> waiting and EVERYTHING else -> running. A pending permission prompt is neither: the turn has not ended, so no Stop fires, and the last signal was a PostToolUse -> running. There is no hook event for 'blocked awaiting approval', so this waiting state is structurally unrepresentable today.

This is the single most misleading state on the board, because it is exactly when the operator's attention IS required. Investigate whether the host emits any pre-approval hook (Claude Code Notification/PreToolUse-deny paths) that could map to waiting; if none exists, consider inferring it from a PostToolUse gap plus an outstanding tool call, or accept the limitation and document it in the adapter capability notes. Must stay agent-agnostic: any mapping belongs in adapter data, not core.

The real remaining gap, found by reproducing the live screenshot: review had a staleness ceiling but needs_action and degraded_active did not, so abandoned attention demands never aged out - the 22H/22H/60D Needs Input cards. Fixed with OPERATIONAL_PROJECTION_ACTIONABLE_STALE_MS (24h, matching review) applied across the legacy path, runtime path, and actionable canonical hints; live process proof always wins so a genuinely waiting agent is never hidden. title: Test suite writes junk sessions into the live Andon database
description:
Root cause of the unexplained 'codex' rows and most of the 1090-row history backlog. src/core/andon.ts defaults to POSTing events at http://127.0.0.1:4318 and only suppresses when ANDON_DISABLED === 'true'; the test runner never sets it. So every full test run that exercises CLI/checkpoint/handoff paths injects sessions into the operator's REAL dashboard.

Hard evidence 2026-07-30: runtime_sessions holds 531 rows with agent_name 'codex' and legacy sessions holds 832, latest 2026-07-30T04:58:35Z - exactly during a tests/run-tests.ts run. Their objectives are unmistakably fixtures: 'First objective', 'Second objective', 'Nothing actionable', 'Handoff traversal probe', 'Track large edit set', 'Track medium edit set', 'Investigate unusual file churn', 'test repo', 'Polish handoff behavior'. The operator does not even have Codex installed, so every one of these is test residue.

Fix: default event emission OFF under test (set ANDON_DISABLED=true in tests/run-tests.ts, and/or point ANDON_API_BASE_URL at a throwaway port), and make the emitter refuse to send when a test environment is detected. Consider also a one-off cleanup of the existing fixture rows, keyed on the known fixture objectives plus the codex agent name.

Note the ANDON_DISABLED check is strict equality against the string 'true', so ANDON_DISABLED=1 silently does nothing - worth accepting 1/yes/on too.

description: Mission Control repeatedly shows the same stale card as active context: "cursor · Parked · Implementing M007: Event Forwarding (Daemon & Wrappers)" even after new work, restarts, and refresh. Live board behavior is still being influenced by stale legacy/session narrative events or stale activeSession carryover instead of authoritative runtime truth. This erodes operator trust in Andon's real-time supervision role.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Fleet live status/objective comes from runtime harness truth (runtime_sessions + runtime_processes + runtime_events) only. 2) A stale legacy objective cannot remain pinned after runtime status changes. 3) "needs_input" and "flowing" states require current runtime evidence (waiting/running + fresh heartbeat), not historical question/resume markers. 4) If runtime feed is unavailable, board shows explicit disconnected/degraded runtime state instead of stale inferred activity. 5) Regression tests cover the stuck-objective scenario and prevent recurrence.

title: Hook-driven checkpoints mint phantom DB-only sessions instead of attaching to the active session
description: 2026-07-29 ~04:09-04:10Z: two sessions (session-2026-07-29T04-09-15-832Z, session-2026-07-29T04-10-08-382Z) appeared in the Andon DB with objective 'Capture work and prepare a clean handoff.' and first events holistic.checkpoint/natural-breakpoint + agent.summary_emitted 'Completion signal detected'. state.json had exactly one activeSession (session-2026-07-28T22-36-59-974Z) the whole time. Correlated with bd close + git commits firing repo git hooks that run holistic capture; the hook-spawned holistic process did not bind to the active session and inferred a fresh session id, creating a permanent needs_input card per commit burst. Investigate the git-hook/beads-hook capture path (user-authored start-holistic/start-andon scripts + HOLISTIC-MANAGED hooks), how it resolves the runtime dir and active session, and why checkpoint inference starts a new session when one is active. Related: holistic-3nn (upstream git-hook auto-start), the hand-written-hooks adoption decision, and the needs_input aging fix in flight.
notes:
CONFIRMED live 2026-07-30 with exact evidence, and NOT fixed by the qd4 aging ceiling. Four phantom sessions were minted inside ten minutes, each a distinct session id rather than an attachment to the active session, all agent_name=claude, all objective 'Capture work and prepare a clean handoff.': session-2026-07-30T04-49-44-916Z, ...T04-50-49-534Z, ...T04-57-13-368Z, ...T04-58-30-452Z. All four project as needs_action/waiting_for_input with actionRequired=true and sit on Mission Control alongside the one real session.

Critically: they are FRESH (signal age ~0h), so holistic-qd4's 24h staleness ceiling does not touch them. That ceiling only clears ABANDONED phantoms; newly minted ones occupy the board immediately. Fixing the minting at the source is therefore still required for a clean board, and is now the top cause of live board noise.

Each mint corresponds to a checkpoint firing (hook-driven UserPromptSubmit checkpoints plus CLI checkpoint/handoff invocations). Likely shares a root with holistic-8j9/holistic-lve: session ownership is not keyed to the active session, so a checkpoint creates rather than joins.

title: HOLISTIC-USER-EDITED marker only protects adapter docs; other derived docs are silently regenerated
description: The generated AGENTS.md promises that adding a HOLISTIC-USER-EDITED line makes Holistic leave a file alone permanently, but writeDerivedDoc never checks isUserAuthoredDoc - only the adapter loop in writeDerivedDocs does. Marking AGENTS.local.md (or HOLISTIC.md etc.) as user-edited does not survive the next writeDerivedDocs call, which fires on every checkpoint including the UserPromptSubmit auto-checkpoint, silently reverting user customizations. Same class as closed holistic-bsz (L-7). Fix: writeDerivedDoc skips user-authored docs universally.

title: L-1: session directory cache does an O(n) stat sweep to avoid an O(n) read
description: readSessionsFromDir builds its cache signature by statSync-ing every JSON file, then returns cached objects on a hit. For the archive directory this stats every historical session on every call, and writeDerivedDocs calls readAllSessions several times per checkpoint. The cache saves parsing but not syscalls. A directory mtime check, or relying on invalidateSessionDirectoryCache alone, would be cheaper.

title: findNearestHolisticRoot treats a bare .holistic dir as a root; ~/.holistic token dir hijacks walk-up
description: The Andon API stores its auth token in ~/.holistic/andon-token, so ~/.holistic exists on any machine running Mission Control. findNearestHolisticRoot only checks directory existence, so any path within 10 levels under the user profile (temp dirs, repos without markers) walks up and resolves the HOME DIRECTORY as the Holistic root. The generated hook scripts already require state.json presence; align the TS walk-up to the same presence check. Surfaced by the worktree-state-resolution fallback test failing once ~/.holistic existed.

title: M-5: package boundaries are decorative; services deep-import each other
description: packages/* and services/* have package.json files but nothing imports through them. Every cross-package reference is a deep relative path into another package source tree, and services/runtime-service imports andon-api/src/runtime-repository.ts directly while sharing its SQLite file. The declared module structure implies isolation that does not exist, and packages/andon-core/dist plus packages/runtime-core/dist are committed build output nothing consumes. Fix: declare npm workspaces, import by package specifier, and move runtime-repository into a shared package.
notes: Partially addressed: runtime-repository.ts moved to services/shared so runtime-service no longer imports andon-api internals. Full npm workspaces migration deliberately deferred: rewriting every deep relative import to a package specifier changes module resolution for the --experimental-strip-types entry points and would require node_modules linking, which is a larger and riskier change than the coupling it removes.
